searchText: Hi. 1.Are Hive Simulators hard coded scenarios or are those providing some higher level abstraction that could be scripted to produce quickly variants of scenarios? 2. Does Hive perform non-functional test (e.g., synchronization speed, transaction throughput, ...) or is it focusing on functional tests? 3. is Hive using internal APIs in clients or is it restricting itself to public APIs and focus on client inter-operability? <@892053833121923094> It really depends on the simulator, all simulators are implemented in golang, but some of them import vectors from outside sources (e.g. https://github.com/ethereum/hive/tree/master/simulators/ethereum/consensus, or https://github.com/ethereum/hive/tree/master/simulators/ethereum/rpc-compat) and others do the hard-coded approach (e.g. https://github.com/ethereum/hive/tree/master/simulators/ethereum/engine) You can also write simulators in different languages No performance testing so far in any of the simulators, most of them do functional testing yes All is public APIs, clients are configured via `HIVE_` parameters, but the way these are handled can be seen in the bash configuration scripts in each client: https://github.com/ethereum/hive/tree/master/clients Thanks, <@892053833121923094>

excerpts.author: marioevz
excerpts.content: It really depends on the simulator, all simulators are implemented in golang, but some of them import vectors from outside sources (e.g. https://github.com/ethereum/hive/tree/master/simulators/ethereum/consensus, or https://github.com/ethereum/hive/tree/master/simulators/ethereum/rpc-compat) and others do the hard-coded approach (e.g. https://github.com/ethereum/hive/tree/master/simulators/ethereum/engine)

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: You can also write simulators in different languages

excerpts.author: marioevz
excerpts.content: No performance testing so far in any of the simulators, most of them do functional testing yes

excerpts.author: marioevz
excerpts.content: All is public APIs, clients are configured via `HIVE_` parameters, but the way these are handled can be seen in the bash configuration scripts in each client: https://github.com/ethereum/hive/tree/master/clients
